plan.title: Confounded lung treated vs control DE (batch-labeled)
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is 6 treated vs 6 control human lung bulk RNA-seq samples (salmon-derived counts, 12000 genes x 12 samples per the counts.csv/metadata.csv), but batch B1 holds all controls and batch B2 holds all treated samples — the batch is perfectly confounded with condition. This is not a design flaw a normalization or correction step can fix: the model matrix ~batch+condition is not full rank, and any batch-removal method (ComBat-seq, limma removeBatchEffect, SVA) would strip the condition effect along with the batch effect, producing a false sense of correction. Per the grounded procedure (rule R-0005), the plan does not fit a batch term and does not apply any batch-correction/removal method. Instead: (1) QC/EDA is run first and explicitly used to characterize how much of the top-variance structure aligns with the batch/condition axis (which, given perfect confounding, is expected to be the same axis) — this is reported as a diagnostic, not a fix; (2) the DESeq2 model uses ~condition only, with treated vs control as the sole contrast; (3) every downstream result (DE gene list, fold changes, enrichment) is explicitly labeled as CONFOUNDED — the analysis cannot distinguish a true treatment effect from a batch/technical effect, and this limitation is carried through every output rather than resolved. Filtering, normalization, the Wald test with apeglm shrinkage, BH FDR with independent filtering, and enrichment (ORA against Hallmark/Reactome, since GSEA on a Wald-statistic ranking was flagged as not permitted for this confounded situation by the knowledge check) all follow the grounded procedure. The report step aggregates diagnostics, gene tables, and enrichment results together with the confounding caveat stated once at the top and repeated with every table.
